display.title: Hashem Chose Me: The Winemakers of Grape Town
display.summary_short: Why did Hashem say 'your G-d' to each Jew at Har Sinai? Three stories, ending with the winemakers of Grape Town, teach that every one of us must do our own part.
display.summary_long: Just after Shavuos, the storyteller asks why the Ten Commandments begin 'I am Hashem your G-d' in the singular, when Hashem was speaking to millions. The answer: Hashem spoke to each Jew as if he were the only one there, so each of us carries the full responsibility and strength to keep the mitzvos. Two short stories set it up. When the Alter Rebbe hosted guests, every helper in the kitchen salted the soup, each thinking no one else would; the Alter Rebbe ate it without complaint, having trained himself under the Maggid not to notice taste. A Rebbe, perhaps the Rebbe Rashab, ate a whole pot of cholent ruined with kerosene so that the kitchen girl would not be shamed. Then the main story: the king will visit Grape Town, famous for its wine, and each resident is to pour a gallon of his best wine into one great barrel. Each one decides a gallon of water will not be noticed, and the king is served pure water. The storyteller ends with the Rebbe's teaching that no one may rely on others to bring Moshiach.
display.lesson: Do not rely on others to do what needs doing: each of us must do our own part, because our mitzvah may be the one that brings the Geulah.
